task_title: Name-vs-ID lookup UX: refresh and catalog push reject API names
task_criteria: PASS when 'musterflow refresh <name>' and 'musterflow catalog push <name>' both resolve a connected API by exact Name (falling back after exact-ID miss) or, when unresolvable, the error names the available ids so the user can act; unit tests cover name resolution on both CLI paths; go build ./... and go test ./... green.

items.criterion: PASS when 'musterflow refresh <name>' and 'musterflow catalog push <name>' both resolve a connected API by exact Name (falling back after exact-ID miss) or, when unresolvable, the error names the available ids so the user can act; unit tests cover name resolution on both CLI paths; go build ./... and go test ./... green.
items.detail: Both CLI paths now resolve name-or-id: internal/cli/commands.go:151 `conn, err := registry.GetByNameOrID(args[0])` (refresh) and internal/cli/root.go:309 (catalog push). internal/app/registry.go:139-146 tries exact ID via r.Get first and only then scans List() for `c.Name == idOrName`; registry.go:158-166 builds the not-found error as `api %q not found; connected: <id> (<name>), ... — use an id or name from 'musterflow list'`, and for an empty registry says `no APIs are connected — run 'musterflow connect <url>'`. Unit tests on both CLI paths: internal/cli/nameorid_test.go TestRefreshResolvesAPIByNameOrID (by-name, by-id) and TestCatalogPushResolvesAPIByNameOrID (by-name, by-id), plus TestUnknownArgErrorNamesConnectedAPIs and TestUnknownArgOnEmptyRegistrySaysHowToConnect — `go test -count=1 -run 'NameOrID|UnknownArg' -v ./internal/cli/` printed `--- PASS: TestRefreshResolvesAPIByNameOrID/by-name`, `--- PASS: TestCatalogPushResolvesAPIByNameOrID/by-name`, `--- PASS: TestUnknownArgErrorNamesConnectedAPIs/refresh-nope`, `--- PASS: TestUnknownArgOnEmptyRegistrySaysHowToConnect/catalog-push-nope`, `ok github.com/.../internal/cli 0.156s`. `go build ./...` exit 0 (no output). `go test -count=1 ./...` exit 0, 11 `ok` lines, zero FAIL/panic.

items.criterion: Exact-ID lookup still wins over a Name match (back-compat: an id that collides with another connection's name resolves by id), and the name fallback only runs after the id miss.
items.detail: internal/app/registry.go:139-146 returns immediately on a successful r.Get(idOrName) and only then falls back to the List() name scan. Covered by internal/app/app_test.go:110 TestRegistry_GetByNameOrID_IDWinsOverName (id "shared-slug" vs another connection's Name "shared-slug" → resolves to ID "shared-slug"); `go test -count=1 ./internal/app/` → `ok github.com/totalwindupflightsystems/musterflow/internal/app 1.256s`.

items.criterion: The dashboard path (dashboardBaseURL != "") must also accept a name: refreshViaDashboard/pushViaDashboard forward the raw arg to /api/apis/<arg> and /api/apis/<arg>/refresh, and the dashboard handlers must resolve name-or-id.
items.detail: internal/cli/register.go:197 POSTs dashboardBaseURL+"/api/apis/"+apiID+"/refresh" and register.go:241 GETs dashboardBaseURL+"/api/apis/"+apiID with the raw argument; internal/dashboard/server.go:207 (GET handler) and server.go:237 (handleRefreshAPI) both call s.registry.GetByNameOrID(id) before acting, so a name works on the dashboard path too. `go test -count=1 ./internal/dashboard/` → `ok ... 1.992s`.

items.criterion: The DF-045 store-unavailable guard must still fire before the new lookup, so a locked/unreadable store reports the lock rather than "api not found".
items.detail: internal/cli/commands.go:145-149 and internal/cli/root.go:303-307 call StoreUnavailable() before GetByNameOrID. `go test -count=1 -run 'Store|Lock' -v ./internal/cli/` printed `--- PASS: TestRefreshFailsWhenStoreIsLocked`, `--- PASS: TestCatalogPushFailsWhenStoreIsLocked`, `--- PASS: TestListFailsWhenStoreIsLocked`, package `ok`.

items.criterion: The refresh path must pass the resolved connection's ID (not the raw name) into app.Refresh, which itself does an id-only registry.Get and would otherwise fail with "get api: not found".
items.detail: internal/cli/commands.go:155 calls `app.Refresh(cmd.Context(), registry, conn.ID)` with the resolved ID; internal/app/refresh.go:14-17 does registry.Get(id) and wraps failures as "get api: %w". TestRefreshResolvesAPIByNameOrID/by-name passes and asserts "✓ Refreshed echo-test-api" and "1.0.0 → 2.0.0", which is only reachable if the name resolved to the id and the spec was re-fetched (the httptest server serves version 2.0.0).

items.criterion: User-facing help/docs must advertise the new accepted spelling (<api-id|name>) on both commands, and the existing Use-string assertions must be updated to match.
items.detail: internal/cli/commands.go:135 `Use: "refresh <api-id|name>"` plus Long text; internal/cli/root.go:293 `Use: "push <api-id|name>"` plus Long text; specs/cli.md:57,335,338 and README.md:104 updated. Existing assertions updated at internal/cli/cli_test.go:1118,1496,1615 and pass (`go test -count=1 ./internal/cli/` → `ok ... 3.499s`).

findings.detection: task row marked status=complete while its own worker_summary states the reported failure is not reproducible
findings.detail: DF-MUSTERFLOW-4 is flipped to "status":"complete" with worker_summary "Not reproducible: GOWORK=off go build ./... exits 0 on the current tree", i.e. the row is closed as fixed when the evidence shows the premise is stale rather than the defect repaired.

findings.detection: completed row retains no commit_hash/guard_result/ci_result while sibling completed rows in the same file carry them
findings.detail: The new DF-MUSTERFLOW-4 complete record has no commit_hash, guard_result, ci_result or completed_at, unlike neighbouring completed rows (e.g. DF-029, DF-033, DF-034) which all record commit_hash/guard_result/ci_result.

findings.detection: detail field type changed from string to object on an existing row
findings.detail: DF-MUSTERFLOW-4's "detail" was a plain string and is rewritten as an object {"evidence":[...],"text":...}, while the other dogfood rows (DF-MUSTERFLOW-1/3/5) keep "detail" as a string — a schema drift for any reader that expects a string.
